messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High GPU queue growth detected in us-west-2 inference pool (redwood-runtime). Trigger: queue_length > 500 for >5m. Auto-paging oncall.sara. Thread_ts: 1812345600

sara: I'm oncall, jumping in. Seeing p95/p99 latency spike and autoscaler not adding capacity beyond cap. looking into root cause.

miguel: FYI I rolled out model v2.2 at 02:00 in us-west-2 (canary -> prod). v2.2 changed default context handling and kv-cache warmup lifecycle. Could be related.

sara: sharing quick metrics snapshot:
```
time,queue_len,active_gpus,autoscale_state
02:03,620,40,at_max
02:07,710,40,throttling
02:10,840,40,burst_queue
```

jin: @sara can you check kv_cache miss rate and per-token throughput after the rollout?

sara: kv_cache_miss_rate jumped ~2% -> ~35% after the v2.2 rollout. Throughput per GPU regressed ~1.4x for long-context requests. Looks like sessions are not reusing kv cache due to a tokenizer/version mismatch and warmup behavior.

paige: @ana from CS — any customer reports yet?

ana: (typo) sorry, ana here — we have two customers reporting increased timeouts: acme-ai and medsys. acme sees timeouts on long-context summarization jobs; medsys reports some 5xx errors. I'm joining the incident bridge.

miguel: mitigation options we discussed: 1) rollback traffic to v2.1 2) increase autoscale cap for us-west-2 temporarily 3) deploy a v2.2 variant with kv-compatibility flag to preserve cache behavior 4) route heavy-context customers to fallback model.

sara: initiating traffic rollback to v2.1 now (traffic-split). Rolling 100% back to v2.1.

deploy-bot: Deploy action: traffic-split rollback initiated by sara at 02:12. Target: v2.1 -> 100%. Status: in_progress.

sara: queue trending down but slowly. will also request manual burst nodes; need infra approval for quota.

jin: starting manual burst scale via runbook:
```
# infra command
k8s-scale nodepool inference-usw2-burst --replicas 10
```

deploy-bot: Nodepool scale requested, pending quota approval.

paige: drafting customer comms: "We experienced increased latency following a model rollout; we rolled back the change and are monitoring. Expecting recovery within 20-30 minutes." Will post to affected accounts.

sara: update 02:20 — queue_len 120, active_gpus 42, autoscale_state: normal. No more throttling. Continue monitoring for errors.

incident-bot: [UPDATE] Severity lowered P2 -> P3. Autoscaler stabilized, throttling cleared, ongoing customer follow-up.

ana: CS notified acme-ai and medsys, both acknowledged and will monitor. acme moved some jobs to lower concurrency while you roll back.

jin: short post-incident notes: root cause appears to be v2.2 kv-cache compatibility change + tokenizer warmup causing cache misses and throughput regression for long-context sessions. Actions: 1) immediate rollback (done), 2) manual burst scale (requested), 3) CS notification (done). Long-term: add kv-compat canary checks, model prewarm for rollouts, and ensure autoscaler headroom for rapid traffic shifts. I'll create INF ticket for follow-up.

sara: handing over to jin for follow-ups; i'm offshift at 03:00. Thanks everyone.

jin: taking post-incident owner. will update runbook and draft postmortem. planning to add a pre-deploy kv-cache compatibility test and a shorter canary window for context-related changes.

incident-bot: Incident resolved and closed at 02:48. Final: two customers impacted with degraded service during ~15 minutes; rollback and burst scaling mitigated load. Postmortem ticket INF-3421 created by jin to track follow-ups."
